question: Which statement best describes the arrangement and movement of particles in a liquid?
options: Closely packed in a disorderly arrangement, sliding past each other
Closely packed in an orderly arrangement, vibrating about fixed positions
Far apart in a random arrangement, moving rapidly in all directions
Widely spaced in a fixed lattice, moving in continuous straight lines
answer: Closely packed in a disorderly arrangement, sliding past each other

question: What happens to the average kinetic energy of gas particles when the gas is heated from 25°C to 80°C?
options: It increases
It decreases
It remains constant
It drops to zero
answer: It increases

question: During the melting of a pure solid, why does the temperature remain constant even though heat energy is continuously supplied?
options: Heat energy is used to overcome attractive forces, increasing average potential energy
Heat energy is converted into kinetic energy, increasing particle speed
Heat energy is lost to the surroundings at the exact same rate
Particles stop moving completely during phase change
answer: Heat energy is used to overcome attractive forces, increasing average potential energy

question: A liquid is cooling and freezing into a solid at its freezing point. Which energy change occurs during this process?
options: Average potential energy decreases while average kinetic energy remains constant
Average kinetic energy decreases while average potential energy increases
Both average kinetic energy and potential energy decrease rapidly
Average potential energy increases while average kinetic energy remains constant
answer: Average potential energy decreases while average kinetic energy remains constant

question: Which state change requires energy to completely overcome the attractive forces between particles?
options: Boiling
Melting
Freezing
Condensing
answer: Boiling

question: Concentrated NH3 and concentrated HCl are placed at opposite ends of a sealed glass tube. A white ring of NH4Cl forms closer to the HCl end. Why?
options: NH3 molecules have a lower relative molecular mass and diffuse faster than HCl
HCl molecules have a lower relative molecular mass and diffuse faster than NH3
NH3 is denser than air and settles faster
HCl molecules move with higher average kinetic energy at room temperature
answer: NH3 molecules have a lower relative molecular mass and diffuse faster than HCl

question: Which row correctly states the relative charges of a proton, neutron, and electron?
options: Proton: +1, Neutron: 0, Electron: -1
Proton: +1, Neutron: -1, Electron: 0
Proton: 0, Neutron: +1, Electron: -1
Proton: -1, Neutron: 0, Electron: +1
answer: Proton: +1, Neutron: 0, Electron: -1

question: What is the overall electrical charge of an atomic nucleus containing 12 protons and 12 neutrons?
A neutral atom of Sodium has a mass number of 23 and an atomic number of 11. How many protons, neutrons, and electrons does it contain?
options: 11 protons, 12 neutrons, 11 electrons
11 protons, 23 neutrons, 11 electrons
12 protons, 11 neutrons, 12 electrons
11 protons, 12 neutrons, 12 electrons
answer: 11 protons, 12 neutrons, 11 electrons

question: An atom has 17 protons, 18 neutrons, and 17 electrons. What is its nucleon number?
An oxide ion, O^{2-}, is formed from an oxygen atom with proton number 8 and mass number 16. How many electrons and neutrons are in O^{2-}?
options: 10 electrons, 8 neutrons
8 electrons, 8 neutrons
10 electrons, 10 neutrons
6 electrons, 8 neutrons
answer: 10 electrons, 8 neutrons

question: An ion X^{3+} has 10 electrons and 14 neutrons. What is the proton number and mass number of element X?
options: Proton number: 13, Mass number: 27
Proton number: 7, Mass number: 21
Proton number: 10, Mass number: 24
Proton number: 13, Mass number: 23
answer: Proton number: 13, Mass number: 27

question: Which statement correctly defines isotopes of the same element?
options: Atoms with the same proton number but different number of neutrons
Atoms with the same nucleon number but different proton numbers
Atoms with the same number of neutrons but different electron numbers
Ions of different elements with the same electronic structure
answer: Atoms with the same proton number but different number of neutrons

question: Why do chlorine isotopes, Chlorine-35 and Chlorine-37, possess identical chemical properties?
options: They have the same number of valence electrons and electronic configuration
They have the same mass number and physical properties
They have the same number of neutrons in their nucleus
They both react with water to produce hydrogen gas at different rates
answer: They have the same number of valence electrons and electronic configuration

question: Carbon-12 and Carbon-14 are isotopes of carbon (proton number 6). How do their subatomic particle counts compare?
options: Carbon-14 has 2 more neutrons than Carbon-12
Carbon-14 has 2 more protons than Carbon-12
Carbon-14 has 2 more electrons than Carbon-12
Carbon-14 has 2 fewer neutrons than Carbon-12
answer: Carbon-14 has 2 more neutrons than Carbon-12

question: Naturally occurring Chlorine exists as 75% Chlorine-35 and 25% Chlorine-37. What is the relative atomic mass of Chlorine?
What is the electronic configuration of a neutral Potassium atom (proton number 19)?
Magnesium has an electronic configuration of 2.8.2. In which Period of the Periodic Table is Magnesium located and why?
options: Period 3, because it has 3 occupied electron shells
Period 2, because it has 2 valence electrons
Period 2, because it forms a 2+ ion
Period 3, because it has 3 valence electrons
answer: Period 3, because it has 3 occupied electron shells

question: An element X has an atomic number of 15. In which Group of the Periodic Table is element X found?
options: Group 15
Group 13
Group 12
Group 17
answer: Group 15

question: Sulfur has a proton number of 16. What are the electronic configurations of a Sulfur atom and a sulfide ion, S^{2-}?
options: Sulfur atom: 2.8.6, Sulfide ion: 2.8.8
Sulfur atom: 2.8.6, Sulfide ion: 2.8.4
Sulfur atom: 2.8.8, Sulfide ion: 2.8.6
Sulfur atom: 2.8.6, Sulfide ion: 2.8.6
answer: Sulfur atom: 2.8.6, Sulfide ion: 2.8.8

question: When a Calcium atom forms a Ca^{2+} ion, what happens to its subatomic particles and nuclear charge?
options: It loses 2 electrons; the nuclear charge remains +20
It gains 2 protons; the nuclear charge increases to +22
It loses 2 protons; the nuclear charge decreases to +18
It gains 2 electrons; the nuclear charge remains +20
answer: It loses 2 electrons; the nuclear charge remains +20

question: The species Na^+, Mg^{2+}, and F^- all have the same electronic configuration (2.8). Which species has the highest number of protons in its nucleus?
options: Na^+
All have the same number of protons

question: Consider the ions N^{3-}, O^{2-}, and F^-. Which statement correctly describes the charge of their nuclei?
options: F^- has a nuclear charge of +9, O^{2-} is +8, and N^{3-} is +7
All three ions have identical nuclear charges of +10
N^{3-} has the highest nuclear charge because it gained 3 electrons
F^- has a negative nuclear charge because it is a halogen
answer: F^- has a nuclear charge of +9, O^{2-} is +8, and N^{3-} is +7

question: During the boiling of pure water at 100°C, heat is continually added but the temperature does not rise. Which combination of statements is correct?
options: Average kinetic energy stays constant; average potential energy increases
Average kinetic energy increases; average potential energy stays constant
Both average kinetic energy and average potential energy increase
Average kinetic energy decreases; attractive forces strengthen
answer: Average kinetic energy stays constant; average potential energy increases
